text:
Sally (Acme): Hey team — we're seeing a lot of truncated SSE streams from /v1/streams. The response ends abruptly and the final JSON is cut off; finish_reason is missing. Happening several times today (started ~2026-03-12 10:02 UTC). Example request id: req-9823df.

Alice (Support): Sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact curl you used and the raw capture you have? Also is this from behind your company's proxy/load balancer? :thinking_face:

Sally (Acme): Yep. Minimal repro I ran from my laptop (macOS 13):

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-13b
```

and here's the tail of the SSE stream we captured (we expect a final `data: { ... "finish_reason": "stop" }`):

```
data: {"id":"resp_abc123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"..."}}]}
data: {"id":"resp_abc123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"more text"}}]}
data: {"id":"resp_abc123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"final bit","finish_reason":
```
It literally cuts mid-json and connection drops. No `data: [DONE]` either.

Ben (SRE): Thanks, Sally. Can you also provide the full request headers and the X-Request-ID (if present)? From the traceback this looks like an upstream connection termination rather than app-level stream finish. Two quick asks:
1) does this correlate with long responses (>30s)?
2) Are you behind an ALB/NGINX/Cloudflare?

Sally (Acme): Yes it happens when generation goes >40s. We're behind our corporate ALB + an nginx reverse proxy in front of the app servers.

Carla (Client Eng): This sounds like the classic proxy idle-timeout / buffering issue. If the proxy buffers until the response is complete it will drop chunked SSE frames. Ben, can you check edge logs for `upstream prematurely closed connection` or `client aborted` events for req-9823df?

Ben (SRE): Pulling logs now. Found an entry around the timestamp:

```
2026-03-12T10:02:43Z [error] 12345#0: *98765 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.0.0.4, server: _, request: "GET /v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-13b HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.0.1.12:8080/", host: "api.redwood.ai", referrer: "-"
```
Followed by: `connection reset by peer` on the TCP socket at 10:02:44. Upstream returned partial bytes. :frowning:  Looks like the upstream (load balancer) closed the tcp stream mid-flight.

Dave (DevEx): For customer-side mitigation we usually recommend: send periodic SSE comments or heartbeat frames so proxies don't see long idle periods. Example server-side heartbeat:

```
: keepalive


```
Some proxies still buffer until they see a flush; for nginx you can set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection "";` and for upstreams ensure `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`. Also adding `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for internal nginx helps.

Ben (SRE): Another quick repro suggestion for Sally — try curl with `--no-buffer` and `-v` to see raw socket behavior. Also set `Connection: keep-alive`. Example:

```
curl -v --no-buffer -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Connection: keep-alive" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-13b
```
If the stream completes with `--no-buffer` but not without it, that strongly points to a buffering intermediary.

Alice (Support): We should also rule out auth/billing interruptions (401/402 midstream). Did your client rotate tokens or hit a rate limit concurrently? Any 401s around X-Request-ID=req-9823df?

Sally (Acme): No auth changes. I checked our audit logs — no 401/402 at that time. Only the TCP reset.

Ben (SRE): FYI I traced the flow across the edge and found that our public ALB idle timeout was set to 60s and our upstream keepalive was lower; when long-running generations have >1 minute gaps between server-sent chunks, some intermediaries will kill the connection. I also saw a rare case where nginx had `proxy_buffering on` in the customer's path and it appears to be aggregating chunks until it reaches a buffer size then failing. Root cause likely configuration mismatch + no heartbeat from client side.

Ben (SRE): Action items:
- Internal: open infra ticket RW-3421 to standardize keepalive/timeouts and ensure edge sends heartbeat-ish comment frames if no payload > 15s.
- For customer (Sally): try the curl `--no-buffer` test and if you control the intermediate nginx set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection \"\";` and `proxy_read_timeout 120s;`. If you can't change the proxy, use the resume/reconnect pattern (client should detect truncated JSON and re-request with last token offset).

Dave (DevEx): Also documenting a recommended snippet for nginx users in our docs: 
```
location /v1/streams/ {
  proxy_pass http://upstream;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_read_timeout 300;
  proxy_send_timeout 300;
  # optional: disable accel buffering
  proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering "no";
}
```

Alice (Support): I've created a support ticket (SUP-12890) and linked RW-3421. Ben/Infra, can you prioritize a short-term mitigation on the edge (increase idle timeout and ensure chunked flush behavior)?

deploy-bot: infra/deploy pipeline started for rw-edge-timeout-fix (PR #4472) — build 522 in progress.

Ben (SRE): Patch rolled out to staging, increased idle timeout to 180s and enabled periodic 15s comment pings from the edge for SSE streams. Will monitor for 24h.

Sally (Acme): Thanks — after we applied `proxy_buffering off` on our side the reproducer now completes and we see the final `finish_reason: \"stop\"`. Great job everyone :tada:

Alice (Support): Awesome — marking this thread resolved for now. If you see any more truncated streams, DM me and we'll reopen SUP-12890. :thumbsup:
